newsitem.title: UK: GEC to sell consumer electronics business - paper.
newsitem.headline: GEC to sell consumer electronics business - paper.

text.p: British defence to electronics giant General Electric Co Plc is holding talks with at least four venture capital groups about disposing of its consumer electronics division, the Sunday Telegraph said.
GEC owns a 50 percent stake in General Domestic Appliances, which includes brand names such as Hotpoint and Creda, and the paper said the disposal would raise around 150 million pounds.
Last week GEC announced it would halve the number of its corporate divisions to five key busness units in order to streamline its operations.
Market watchers immediately said the industrial apparatus and consumer electronics divisions -- both said to have low margins and tough markets -- were two likely candidates for divestment.
The newspaper said GEC wanted to auction off the business to the highest bidder. Negotiations were at an early stage and the potential buyers were loath to be named, it added.
It was not immediately possible to contact GEC for comment.
